title: Why Do Your Ears RING After a Concert? 🎸
description:
You headbang at a concert, and now your ears are ringing. That ring probably isn't coming from your ears at all: it's your brain, turning its own volume up. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

How it works: loud music batters the tiny hair cells in your inner ear, the cells that turn sound into nerve signals, so less sound reaches your brain. The leading idea (not settled yet) is that the brain's hearing areas then turn up their own gain to make up for it, and at that volume they start hearing their own background activity: a ring or a hiss that isn't out there. Even people with normal hearing hear something like it in a dead-silent room: in a 1953 test, 94 percent of 80 people sitting in a soundproof booth heard buzzing or ringing (and 83 percent in a 2008 repeat). After a gig the ringing usually fades within a day or two, but hair cells that die don't grow back in people, while birds can regrow theirs. Wear earplugs at loud gigs, and if the ringing doesn't go away, see a doctor.
